questions.title: INNER JOIN Keeps Matches
questions.description: What does the snippet return?
questions.Option2: Only owner-pet pairs that actually match
questions.Option3: Every pet, even without an owner
questions.codesnippet:
SELECT o.name, p.name
FROM owners o JOIN pets p ON p.owner_id = o.id;

questions.title: LEFT JOIN Padding
questions.description: In a LEFT JOIN, what happens to left-side rows with no right-side match?
questions.Option3: They survive with NULLs in the right-side columns

questions.title: RIGHT JOIN Keeps
questions.description: A RIGHT JOIN guarantees which rows survive?
questions.Option1: All rows of the right-side table
questions.Option2: All rows of the left-side table

questions.title: FULL OUTER JOIN Keeps
questions.description: What does a FULL OUTER JOIN return?
questions.Option4: All rows from both sides, matched where possible

questions.title: ON Clause Role
questions.description: What does the ON clause do in a join?
questions.Option1: Filters rows after the join completes
questions.Option2: Defines the match condition between the two tables

questions.title: USING Requirement
questions.description: What does JOIN ... USING(city) require of the two tables?
questions.Option3: A column with the same name in both tables
questions.Option4: It only works on primary keys

questions.title: Rows Per Pet
questions.description: Each pet has exactly one owner. owners JOIN pets ON p.owner_id = o.id produces how many rows per pet?
questions.Option4: One row for the whole clinic

questions.title: Where JOIN Lives
questions.description: Which clause does JOIN immediately follow in a SELECT?

questions.title: Anti Join Pattern
questions.description: Which query finds owners with no pets?
questions.Option3: LEFT JOIN pets, then WHERE p.id IS NULL
questions.Option4: SELECT * FROM owners GROUP BY id

questions.title: Three Table Chain
questions.description: How do you join owners, pets and visits correctly?
questions.Option1: All three tables in a single ON clause
questions.Option2: A comma-separated FROM list is the only way
questions.Option4: Chain the JOINs, giving each its own ON condition

questions.title: USING Output Shape
questions.description: What does SELECT * after USING(city) show for the city column?
questions.Option1: city appears once in the output
questions.Option3: USING also needs an ON clause
questions.codesnippet:
SELECT o.name, b.branch_name
FROM owners o JOIN clinic_branches b USING(city);

questions.title: WHERE Collapses LEFT JOIN
questions.description: A LEFT JOIN is followed by WHERE p.age > 0 on the right table. What is the effect?
questions.Option1: It behaves like a FULL OUTER JOIN
questions.Option2: It behaves like an INNER JOIN — non-matching left rows are removed by the WHERE

questions.title: ON Vs WHERE In Outer Joins
questions.description: Owners with no pet older than 3 — do they survive the snippet's LEFT JOIN?
questions.Option1: No — the ON filter removes them
questions.Option2: Only if they own a puppy
questions.Option3: Yes — with NULL pet columns, because the extra condition lives in ON
questions.codesnippet:
SELECT o.name FROM owners o
LEFT JOIN pets p ON p.owner_id = o.id AND p.age > 3;

questions.title: RIGHT JOIN Rewrite
questions.description: owners o RIGHT JOIN pets p ON p.owner_id = o.id equals which left join?
questions.Option1: pets p LEFT JOIN owners o on the same condition — the same query with the tables swapped
questions.codesnippet:
SELECT p.name, o.name
FROM pets p LEFT JOIN owners o ON o.id = p.owner_id;

questions.title: Join Chain Evaluation
questions.description: How does SQLite evaluate chained joins like A JOIN B ON ... JOIN C ON ...?
questions.Option1: All ON clauses merge into one condition
questions.Option2: Left to right — each ON applies to the result built so far

questions.title: INNER JOIN With True ON
questions.description: What is INNER JOIN x ON 1 = 1 equivalent to?

questions.title: FULL JOIN NULL Sides
questions.description: In a FULL OUTER JOIN result, which sides of an output row can be NULL-padded?
questions.Option3: The left, the right, or both
questions.Option4: Never — FULL joins drop NULL rows

questions.title: Gap Rows Test
questions.description: In the chained FULL OUTER JOIN audit, which WHERE clause isolates BOTH gap kinds (ownerless pets and visitless pets)?
questions.Option1: p.id IS NULL OR v.id IS NULL

questions.title: RIGHT FULL JOIN Version
questions.description: Since which SQLite version are RIGHT and FULL OUTER JOIN available?
questions.Option3: Only with the join extension loaded

questions.title: Chained LEFT JOIN Shape
questions.description: One pet has no visits and one owner has no pets; all pets have owners. How many rows does the snippet return, and which are NULL-padded?
questions.Option2: 13 rows — only the petless owner row survives
questions.Option3: An error — two LEFT JOINs cannot chain
questions.Option4: 14 rows — the petless owner and the visitless pet appear with NULLs
questions.codesnippet:
SELECT o.name, p.name, v.reason
FROM owners o
LEFT JOIN pets p ON p.owner_id = o.id
LEFT JOIN visits v ON v.pet_id = p.id;
